intent: Implement and document a production-oriented C11 stackful coroutine library and an epoll-based TCP L4 forwarder for Linux x86-64 on ssh d2, with bounded ownership and reproducible correctness and performance evidence.

evidence: learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/evidence/raw/l4/proxy-4-client.json:363-369: socket 9 reports "bytes": 0 and "bits_per_second": 0 across the complete 3.000032-second sender result; its three measured intervals at lines 155-160, 218-223, and 281-286 are also all zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a bounded ready-task dispatch budget, poll epoll with timeout 0 when the budget is exhausted, and add a deterministic yielding-task versus readable-FD regression.
findings.title: Ready tasks can starve all I/O waiters
findings.why_it_matters: The scheduler polls file-descriptor readiness only after the ready queue becomes empty. A throughput coroutine that calls rco_yield() immediately requeues itself, so sustained runnable traffic can keep accept, signal, and other connection waiters asleep indefinitely. The checked-in four-flow benchmark already records one proxied flow sending zero bytes for the full three-second measurement, so this is an observed fairness and tail-latency failure rather than a theoretical optimization.

findings.suggested_fix: Require exactly the requested stream count and nonzero bytes for every iperf sender and receiver before recording a sample.
findings.title: Benchmark accepts fully stalled streams
findings.why_it_matters: The benchmark treats a nonzero aggregate as a valid sample without checking individual parallel streams. Three of the five supplied proxy runs contain a sender that transferred zero bytes for the full measurement, yet all three contribute to the reported median, so the evidence gate can pass while 25% of flows are starved.

evidence: learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/src/rco.c:710-711: "(void)task->entry(task->argument);\n        task->state = task->cancel_requested ? RCO_TASK_CANCELLED : RCO_TASK_DONE;"
learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/src/rco.c:1085-1087: "struct rco_fd_watch *watch = rco_watch_get(runtime, fd, true);\n    if (watch == NULL) {\n        return -ENOMEM;"

Trigger chain: first watch allocation or listener epoll registration fails -> accept_entry returns the error -> trampoline discards it and removes the task -> signal task remains blocked -> runtime and process stay alive without an accept loop.
findings.suggested_fix: Route unexpected listener wait errors through app_fail() and add injected registration-failure coverage.
findings.title: Accept failure leaves a live dead proxy
findings.why_it_matters: An unexpected listener wait failure terminates only the accept coroutine. The runtime discards task return values, so the signal coroutine keeps the process alive and the listening socket remains open; health checks can still connect into the backlog while no connection is ever accepted or forwarded.

evidence: learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/src/rco.c:651-652: "if (writer != NULL && writer != reader && write_ready) {\n        rco_task_wake(runtime, writer, 0, RCO_EVENT_WRITE);"
Trigger chain: one task requests READ|WRITE -> it occupies both watch slots -> kernel reports EPOLLOUT without EPOLLIN -> read_ready is false and writer != reader is false -> no wake occurs.
findings.first_evidence: learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/src/rco.c:651-652: "if (writer != NULL && writer != reader && write_ready) {\n        rco_task_wake(runtime, writer, 0, RCO_EVENT_WRITE);"
findings.suggested_fix: Handle reader == writer as a dedicated case: combine whichever requested readiness bits fired and wake the task once when the combined mask is nonzero. Add an EPOLLOUT-only socket test for RCO_EVENT_READ | RCO_EVENT_WRITE.
findings.title: Combined read/write wait misses write-only readiness
findings.why_it_matters: The public event mask accepts READ|WRITE, but when only EPOLLOUT arrives the same task is both reader and writer: the read branch is skipped and the write branch rejects writer == reader. The coroutine then hangs forever or times out even though its requested write event is ready.

triage_groups.title: Scheduler fairness and measurement fidelity
triage_groups.context: The scheduler starvation bug is visible in zero-byte iperf streams that the benchmark accepted.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix #1 and its regression first, then harden the per-stream gate in #5 and rerun evidence.
triage_groups.why: One runtime defect and one silent-pass guard share the same observed symptom.

residual_risks: Normal readiness cycles delete and re-add epoll registrations; EPOLLONESHOT rearming may reduce hot-path epoll_ctl calls but needs a dedicated benchmark.
Connection-cap rejection can consume CPU under a sustained accept flood; no overload benchmark exists yet.
A CLOCK_MONOTONIC failure can leave timer waiters spinning; this narrow failure path lacks fault injection.
The generic TCP proxy has no established-connection idle timeout; operators must choose whether indefinite connections are part of their protocol contract.
testing_gaps: Strengthen the deep-stack checksum at every recursion level.
Add an EOF-delayed backend half-close test.
Add stale numeric-FD reuse coverage for generation rejection.
Make the context benchmark verify exact task and switch counts.
